derivation: probably from H2492 (חָלַם) (in the sense of hardness);

occurrences.text: He made him ride on the high places of the earth, that he might eat the increase of the fields; and he made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock;
He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.
Which turned the rock into a standing water, the flint into a fountain of waters.
For the Lord God will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
